correctness.rationale: Monodromy/branch equivalence and the braid action establish an exact bijection with spanning balanced multisets. Subspace Möbius inversion and the five verified GL_3(F_2) cycle types establish rationality. The standalone standard-library verifier constructs the finite rational summands and uses a common denominator E of degree 70, exact divisibility by the proposed denominator, and exact matching through degree 70, which proves the infinite rational identity. Riemann–Hurwitz and pole orders yield the claimed genus/asymptotic. Independent small-r brute orbit counts agree but are not used to infer the universal theorem.

originality.rationale: The evaluated all-branch-length rank-three binary rational series, not the standard Nielsen/zero-sum reduction or prior general enumeration method, is the single assessed contribution. Primary literature comparisons identify general theory (Broughton–Wootton), the disjoint rank-two odd-prime setting (Weaver), and finite-genus data (Disney-Hogg–Zuev), without an identical or dominating closed expression. An implicit historic derivation cannot be ruled out.
residual_risks: The general Broughton–Wootton enumeration framework can in principle imply every individual coefficient; an unnoticed earlier explicit specialization to this exact rational function may exist.
Paulhus finite-genus source data were only assessed through the originating paper, not exhaustively inspected.
Topological equivalence here allows Aut(G) and unlabelled branch points; alternative conventions count different objects.

value.rationale: This is a complete, exact, naturally defined counting invariant for one infinite family of genus-varying noncyclic abelian covers. The rational form provides every genus count and its sharp sixth-degree asymptotic, while prior finite-genus datasets and general classification methods do not provide this precise evaluated benchmark. The seven-color Fano-plane parity condition makes the calculation structurally nontrivial rather than a renaming or arbitrary numerical slice.
